newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb blast in mosque kills three in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast in mosque kills three in Kashmir.

text.p: A bomb exploded in a mosque on Tuesday in India's troubled Kashmir region, killing three people and injuring at least four, police said.

The bomb went off in a mosque in Maharaja Gunj in downtown Srinagar while Moslem worshippers were waiting to break their holy Ramadan fast on Tuesday evening, they said. Srinagar is the summer capital of the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
Ramadan, the Moslem month of fasting, began on Saturday.
No separatist group claimed responsibility for the blast. The injured have been taken to hospital, police said.
More than 20,000 people have died in Kashmir since 1990, when an armed Islamic revolt against New Delhi erupted in the state, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province.
Violence continues unabated in the Himalayan region three months after state assembly elections -- the first since the revolt began in 1990 -- restored local rule.
According to police, there were 40 bomb explosions and 55 grenade attacks in November and December, up from 35 explosions and 38 attacks in July and August.
More than 300 people have died in insurgency-related incidents in the Kashmir Valley over the past two months, police said.
